$comment: The cross-language mirror inventory (docs/FRONTEND.md, Cross-language mirrors).
Every mirror that survives #236's payload contract and #239's module extraction is
listed here with the proof that holds it. `tests/test_mirrors.py` derives candidate
mirrors from the tree with `tests/cross_language_mirrors.py` and holds this file to
the result in both directions, so an undeclared mirror and a stale declaration each
fail `make check`.
`evidence` is what the derivation found, and is the drift detector for a mirror
whose whole content is a shared string: change the words on either side and the
declared evidence stops being derived. It is empty for a mirror the derivation
cannot see -- arithmetic and structure share no words -- which is why those carry a
generated fixture instead.
`proof` values:
parity-fixture       cases in tests/js/fixtures/mirror-parity.json, generated by
tests/mirror_parity.py and asserted by
tests/js/mirror-parity.test.mjs.
lens-parity-fixture  cases in tests/js/fixtures/lens-parity.json.
markup-parity        the audited-page region diff in tests/js/*-markup-parity.test.mjs
renders the lit half and compares it with the Jinja half.
shared-literal       the mirror is one constant string; the derived text evidence
is itself the check, because changing either side removes it.
payload-carried      the rule's preferred outcome: the server publishes the value
and the client reads it rather than recomputing it.

share-percentage-label.note: A whole percentage over exact integer arithmetic on both sides. Shares no words with its server half, so only the fixture can see it drift; the fixture's boundary shares are the exact halves a float round would land on the wrong side of.

no-majority.note: At or below half, not merely behind the leader. The threshold is a comparison rather than a string, so the shared qualifier text alone would not catch a flipped inequality.

share-accessible-label.note: The meter's spoken label. The two sides disagreed about a race with no share until this fixture reached one: the client reused the meter's visible N/A where the server says 'not available'. Fixed in #240 on the client, which is the side that had invented the wording.

support-summary.note: Mirrored only in the no-lens branch; with a selection the client states a count the server has no wording for.

support-summary-compact.note: Two words and a number, so the derivation's prose filter cannot see it. A reviewed entry rather than a derived one.

recommendation-label.server: publication/builder.py recommendation_label, held by models.py validate_display_semantics
recommendation-label.note: Sole leader, tie, and insufficiency each choose different words. The fixture's panels reach all three from real bundles.

race-detail-support-summary.note: The client names its counterpart in a comment. That claim is what put this entry here; the fixture is what makes it true.

race-detail-accessible-summary.note: The mirror #240 was opened for. The audited value is carried in the payload since #236; this recomputes it while a lens is active, which is why the function survives.

counting-summary.server: guide.html.j2 lens banner and sources.html.j2 page count
counting-summary.note: Template text rather than a function, so the fixture reads its expectation out of the committed audited pages.

tallying-source-count.note: The number inside the counting sentence, and its own mirror: the guide counts contributing consensus sources in Jinja while the client counts non-comparison payload sources. Two predicates over two collections that have to reach one total, or the banner changes the instant a reader touches the page.

comparison-percentage-label.note: The one FRONTEND.md recorded as owed. Markup parity reaches only the baseline column's share; a category column's share is computed on the client and rendered nowhere on the audited page, so the boundary cases are the only way to see it.

comparison-row-differs.note: Set logic over lead sets, sharing no text at all. Neutral cells are the interesting half: a blank column must neither agree nor create a difference.

compare-fragment-encoding.note: The encoding mirror, which § Cross-language mirrors names as a category and which is the only one left. Python composes the preset fragments the Comparisons page renders as links; the client composes the same fragment for every state change after that. Both spell the same parameter names in the same canonical order, the same cmp=1 schema version, and the same twelve-character panel-hash prefix — panel_hash[:12] against HASH_PREFIX_LENGTH = 12. It shares no display text and neither side names the other, so no derivation signal can see it: this entry exists because a reviewer put it there, which is the floor-not-ceiling rule doing its work. Drift here is quiet rather than loud — a preset link decodes as stale_version and the page loads on its default columns instead of the ones the link asked for.
compare-fragment-encoding.known_asymmetry: The two sides agree on every column set the server produces, but not on which sets are legal. compare-url.mjs guards encodeCompareFragment with MIN_COLUMNS = 2 and MAX_COLUMNS = 3; comparison_fragment has no matching guard. Every preset in rendering/documents.py asks for two columns, so nothing is wrong today, but a one- or four-column preset would render a link the client refuses to decode. The golden cases stay inside the range both sides admit rather than asserting a shape only one of them has an opinion about.

lens-scoring.note: The pattern every other entry follows. Its fixture predates this inventory and is generated by publication/lens_parity.py.

meter-unavailable-label.server: guide.html.j2 empty meter, asserted by rendering/validation.py _html_semantic_values
meter-unavailable-label.note: The meter's visible text for a race with no share, and the sibling of the divergence this ticket found one line away: the spoken label says 'not available' while both sides show 'N/A'. The server writes the literal in the template rather than in a function, but validation.py already spells the whole rule as an expression — 'N/A' if percentage_whole is None else percentage_label — so that is the oracle for both branches. The audited dataset renders no null-share race, so markup parity cannot reach this any more than it could reach the spoken half.

no-majority-pill.note: A third spelling of the qualifier, after 'No majority.' in the accessible summaries and 'No majority ·' in the dialog kicker. This one is inside a card region guide-markup-parity diffs against the audited page, so the rendered markup is what holds it.

sources-also-in-tag.note: The tags themselves are payload-carried (#248); the two words introducing them are not, and sources-markup-parity diffs the region that renders them.

blank-comparison-cell-dash.note: The em dash a cell shows when a source published no endorsement. Inside the row groups compare-markup-parity diffs. Its `title` explanation is an attribute, which neither side's scan reads — the markup diff does compare attributes, so the pair is still held.

view-toggle-labels.note: The filter status line names the current view using the same two words the toggle is labelled with, so a reader hears the label they just pressed. The server renders the control, the client composes the announcement, and neither reads the other's text.

comparison-race-heading.note: The other heading in the same row as all-sources-column-label, and unguarded for the same reason: the comparison head is deliberately outside the markup-parity claim. One word, so the derivation is the whole check — and it took widening the scan past its space-requiring filter to see it at all.

default-comparison-columns.note: Category codes, not display text — the scan reaches them because a capitalized token is not syntax. The payload publishes every category with its code and label, and the client resolves labels through it; these literals are a preference order for which columns to offer first, which the server does not compute. Nothing is spelled twice except the codes themselves, and tests/test_client_payload_types.py holds the client to the published catalog.

grade-vocabulary.server: scoring/models.py Grade, via the payload generator
grade-vocabulary.note: The grade strings have one generator, as § Shared names requires: the client's ComputedGrade is generated from the audited engine's Grade, and tests/test_client_payload_types.py fails when the two vocabularies stop matching. The client compares against these strings rather than redefining them.

race-detail-lens-kicker.note: Three words the dialog shows above a candidate, written as a Jinja branch on one side and a ternary on the other. Note the qualifier is spelled 'No majority ·' here and 'No majority.' in the accessible summaries — two spellings of one idea, each mirrored separately, which is why both keys are declared. tests/page_parity.py empties the dialog interior when it builds the audited page, so no markup diff can reach these; the words are the whole mirror and the derivation is what holds them.

race-detail-lens-count.note: The sole leader's contributing count, and the parenthetical that appears when a co-endorsement splits its support. Same dialog interior as the kicker above and the same reason nothing else covers it. The evidence keys carry the placeholder positions as well as the words, so a count that moved within the sentence would fail too.

comparison-control-status.server: compare.html.j2, the status argument to election_controls
comparison-control-status.note: The Comparisons control bar's status line. The server composes it in a Jinja concatenation passed as a macro argument; the client assigns its own with textContent, outside the lit regions compare-markup-parity diffs. Both sentences reduce to one template, so a word or a placeholder moving on either side alone stops the evidence being derived.

all-sources-column-label.note: The comparison head is deliberately outside the markup-parity claim, because the audited page cannot render column controls that do nothing without JavaScript. What is left to agree on is two words, and the derivation sees them.

outside-scope-cell-text.note: Also inside the region compare-markup-parity diffs, but only for a race the audited data puts a source outside. The literal is checked whether or not that race exists.

audited-insufficient-note.server: guide.html.j2 race card, asserted by rendering/validation.py
evidence: text:Too few endorsements to measure agreement.
audited-insufficient-note.note: The audited dataset grades no race insufficient, so no markup diff can render this note. Its words are the whole mirror, so the derivation is the check.

filter-scope-fallback-label.note: The payload publishes every scope label from the same generator the template renders, so the client reads the label rather than composing it. The literal that remains is a fallback for a select value the payload does not know, which the rendered markup cannot produce.

$comment: Mirrors #240 was written against that no longer exist, recorded so the next reader
does not go looking for them. Each is the 'prefer deleting a mirror' rule applied.
deleted.renderer.py _race_detail_accessible_summ: Not deleted, relocated: #242 split renderer.py, and this is rendering/context.py race_detail_accessible_summary. Its client half survives and is fixtured.
deleted.audited accessible summary: #236 moved the audited value into the payload as audited_accessible_summary, so nothing recomputes it to restore the default view.
deleted.audited candidate order: #236 publishes the order the renderer rendered; the client no longer re-sorts.
deleted.sources tree strings: #248 gave the tree to lit reading payload strings, so its endorsement counts and category tags have no second implementation.
deleted.election-day phrasing: rendering/shell.py publishes the full and short dates as data attributes; election-day.mjs chooses copy but formats no date.
deleted.source participation label: rendering/payload.py source_participation_label feeds the template and the payload from one definition, replacing a Jinja macro.
